title: Accelerating Safe Reinforcement Learning with Massive Parallelism
claim: Massively parallel training reaches comparable final performance and constraint satisfaction as standard training, in far less wall-clock time.
layout: 2 stacked blocks of 2x6 line-plot grids, wall-clock left, samples right
description: Two stacked blocks, (a) Point/Goal and (b) Car/Goal. Each block is a 2x6 grid of line plots. Rows show Reward (up is better) and Cost (down is better). The left three columns plot against wall-clock time in minutes, and the right three plot against total environment steps (up to 40e6). Columns are the algorithms CPO, CRPO and TRPO-Lag. A grey line with circle markers is the standard baseline. Green lines in three shades, with circle, triangle and cross markers, are the massive-parallel runs with 2k, 4k and 8k environments. A red dashed horizontal line marks the cost limit. A shared legend sits below each block. In the time plots the green curves rise steeply and finish early. In the sample plots they are slower than the grey baseline. The eye goes to the green curves hugging the left axis.
caption: Wall-clock wise and total sample wise learning curves of all algorithms on the Goal task. Columns correspond to CPO, CRPO, and TRPO-Lag. Markers are shown every 100 epochs and report trailing 10-epoch averages, and the horizontal line marks the cost limit.
abstract: We investigate the problem of scaling safe reinforcement learning (safe RL) to massively parallel training regimes, where a large number of environments are exe- cuted with short rollout horizons. Although this setting improves data throughput and wall-clock efficiency, it creates a mismatch with constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs), whose safety constraints are defined over full-episode cost returns. We address this mismatch by analyzing staggered environment resets as a phase-mixture distribution over short trajectory segments. This analysis charac- terizes the bias induced by phase coverage and motivates a phase-aggregated cost estimator that reconstructs episode-level cost estimates from short rollout batches. We further incorporate finite-sample uncertainty and distribution mismatch into a constraint-tightening framework, yielding a scalable Safe RL method compatible with on-policy optimization. Using an MJX-based implementation of Safety Gym, our experiments show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to non-massively parallel implementations while substantially reducing wall-clock training time.
